In brief: the claim is **false as stated**. The 85% round-trip figure exceeds even the lossless Carnot ceiling (~62–64%) for the resistive-heating architecture the stated 290–565°C temperatures describe, and no real deployed or vendor-specified system (Siemens Gamesa's rock ETES at 45%, Malta's heat-pump PHES at 53–65%) comes close. The 85%+ figures that do appear in the literature (DOE's >93%, CSP's 95%) are measuring heat retained as heat, not electricity recovered — the claim conflates the two. At 5 MWh the molten-salt system is also roughly 4–10x more expensive per kWh than lithium-ion, dominated by the power block's poor small-scale economics, so it loses on cost as well. Overall confidence: MEDIUM (the efficiency falsification is HIGH-confidence; the cost analysis is capped at MEDIUM by one unread citation).
